def: Coating of a microbe with molecules such as IgG or C3b that make it easier for phagocytes to engulf. In type II hypersensitivity, opsonized cells are destroyed by macrophages.
The oily resin in poison ivy, oak and sumac that triggers allergic contact dermatitis. It acts as a hapten causing a type IV (T cell-mediated) hypersensitivity reaction.
Fragmentation of the nucleus into pieces during cell death, as occurs in apoptosis and necrosis.
Dissolution of the nucleus and fading of its staining during cell death, caused by DNase activity in necrosis.
Inflammation of a single joint. Causes include septic arthritis, gout, pseudogout and trauma.
A flow cytometry assay in which neutrophils that make a respiratory burst oxidize dihydrorhodamine to a fluorescent product. It diagnoses chronic granulomatous disease, where fluorescence is absent.
A muscarinic agonist that stimulates saliva and tear secretion. It treats dry mouth and eyes in Sjogren syndrome.
Tight, thickened, shiny skin of the fingers with limited motion, a feature of systemic sclerosis and CREST syndrome.
Bead-like enlargement of the costochondral junctions of the ribs in rickets, caused by excess osteoid deposition.
Softening of the skull bones in infants that yields like a ping-pong ball under pressure. It is a sign of rickets and can also be benign in newborns.
A fragment of dead bone surrounded by infected tissue in chronic osteomyelitis. It appears as a dense piece within a lytic lesion on x-ray.
A finger deformity with flexion of the proximal interphalangeal joint and hyperextension of the distal joint. It is seen in rheumatoid arthritis.
Describes a protein in which arginine has been converted to citrulline. Anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide (anti-CCP) antibodies are highly specific for rheumatoid arthritis.
Located around the edges of muscle fascicles. Perifascicular atrophy is the characteristic finding in dermatomyositis.
Relating to the perimysium, the connective tissue sheath around muscle fascicles. Dermatomyositis shows perimysial inflammation.
Relating to the front of the elbow. Atopic dermatitis in adults often involves the antecubital fossae.
Located behind the ear. Retroauricular lymphadenopathy is characteristic of rubella.
Located beneath a nail. Subungual melanoma and subungual hematoma are examples.
Describes a tumor that cannot be completely removed by surgery because of location, extent or spread.
A ring of fine scale at the edge of a skin lesion. It marks the herald patch of pityriasis rosea.
Inflamed bumps from shaved hairs that curl back and penetrate the skin, common in people with curly hair on the beard area.
A direct thrombin inhibitor given by subcutaneous injection for prevention of deep vein thrombosis after hip surgery.
A modified factor Xa decoy that binds and reverses factor Xa inhibitors such as rivaroxaban and apixaban.
Growth of endothelial cells over a coronary stent. Delayed endothelialization with drug-eluting stents prolongs the risk of stent thrombosis and the need for dual antiplatelet therapy.
A suprahyoid muscle with two bellies. The anterior belly (first arch, mandibular nerve) and posterior belly (second arch, facial nerve) open the jaw and elevate the hyoid.
An infrahyoid strap muscle from the sternum to the hyoid that depresses the hyoid bone. It is supplied by the ansa cervicalis.
An infrahyoid strap muscle with two bellies that depresses the hyoid. It is supplied by the ansa cervicalis.
An infrahyoid strap muscle from the sternum to the thyroid cartilage that depresses the larynx. It is supplied by the ansa cervicalis.
Small, recessed lower jaw. It is seen in Treacher Collins syndrome and Pierre Robin sequence.
A steroidal irreversible aromatase inhibitor that blocks estrogen synthesis. It treats hormone receptor-positive breast cancer in postmenopausal women.
A drug that blocks progesterone receptors. Mifepristone and ulipristal are examples used for abortion and emergency contraception.
A thrombopoietin receptor-binding peptide (TPO analog) given by injection to raise platelet counts in immune thrombocytopenia.
An oral thrombopoietin receptor agonist that increases platelet production in immune thrombocytopenia and aplastic anemia.
Red blood cells shaped like a teardrop (dacrocytes), seen in myelofibrosis, thalassemia and marrow infiltration.
A payment model in which a provider receives a fixed amount per patient per period regardless of services used.
A powered rotating blade with suction used to remove tissue endoscopically, as in treating laryngeal papillomatosis.
A radiofrequency ablation method that removes tissue using low heat, used in tonsillectomy and for laryngeal papillomas.
Surrounding the gallbladder. Pericholecystic fluid on ultrasound suggests cholecystitis.
Located outside the colon. CT colonography can reveal extracolonic findings such as aneurysms or masses.
Heritable changes in gene expression that do not alter the DNA sequence, such as DNA methylation and histone acetylation.
A third variable linked to both exposure and outcome that distorts their apparent association. It is controlled by randomization, matching or stratification.
A monoclonal antibody against the IL-4 receptor alpha subunit, blocking IL-4 and IL-13 signaling. It treats atopic dermatitis and asthma.
Testing airway reactivity by inhaling a trigger such as methacholine or exercise. A positive result supports asthma.
A small wrist (carpal) bone in the distal row, between the trapezium and capitate.
A pyramid-shaped carpal bone on the ulnar side of the proximal wrist row, between the lunate and pisiform.
The largest carpal bone, in the center of the distal wrist row. It articulates with the third metacarpal.
An upper arm muscle under the biceps that flexes the elbow. It is supplied by the musculocutaneous nerve.
Bony projections above the condyles of the humerus (medial and lateral) or femur. Medial epicondylitis is golfer elbow and lateral is tennis elbow.
Rotation of the forearm so the palm faces up. The biceps brachii and supinator muscle perform it.
A small, thin calf muscle with a long tendon, supplied by the tibial nerve. Its tendon can rupture.
